biography.plain_text: Hungarian-born Canadian entrepreneur Peter Munk founded Barrick Gold, building much of his fortune through gold mining. His earlier ventures included Clairtone, the stereo manufacturer launched with funding from his father-in-law, and a Pacific hotel business. Based in Toronto, he also developed commercial property and became a major donor to Canadian institutions.

long_biography.plain_text:
Barrick Gold founder Peter Munk and his wife, Melanie, helped establish the cardiac centre bearing his name at Toronto General Hospital. Their gifts equipped the centre and endowed research chairs in fields including aortic disease and advanced cardiac therapies. Munk linked his donations to gratitude for Canada, where he had arrived as a young immigrant and studied electrical engineering at the University of Toronto.

At his alma mater, the couple supported the creation of the Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy. They also funded the Munk Debates, bringing public figures and thinkers to Toronto to discuss international issues before an audience.
